newsitem.title: INDONESIA: South Africa woos Indonesian business at seminar.
newsitem.headline: South Africa woos Indonesian business at seminar.

text.p: South Africa held its first trade promotion seminar in Indonesia on Friday to tell the Indonesian business community about trade and investment opportunities in South and southern Africa.

South Africa's ambassador in Jakarta, Sydney Kubheka, said the two countries were negotiating agreements covering double taxation, investment protection, cooperation in science and technology and an air services pact.
He said he hoped agreements would soon be in place.
"South Africa represents an excellent business partner that is worthy of serious consideration by Indonesian businessmen," he told about 100 business leaders at the one-day seminar.
He said total bilateral trade had jumped to more than $200 million last year from $60 million in 1994, the year diplomatic relations were established.
Two-way trade was more than $200 million in the first seven months of this year.
Kubheka said mining was one of the key areas for cooperation between the two countries". He specified technical transfers, turnkey projects and exchanges of personnel.

Jakarta's ambassador in Pretoria, Rachadi Iskandar, mentioned Indonesia's export potential in palm oil, rubber, textiles, footwear, garments and wood products. South Africa, he said, could provide Indonesia with some minerals.
Both ambassadors also stressed the well-developed financial, legal and communications infrastucture in South Africa, which they said made it a gateway to the rest of sub-Saharan Africa.

Durban businessman Schabir Shaik, executive chairman of Nkobi Holdings, said there were diverse investment opportunities in South Africa, ranging from telecommunications, transport infrastructure and health care to housing development and the hotel and leisure industry.
He said that in KwaZulu-Natal, for example, "there is a drastic shortage of five-star quality hotels".
"There are large opportunities in the hotel and leisure industries in South Africa," he said.
